Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal01–03 · Purpose, Questions, Principles
Section 01

Purpose

Turn Pipeline Explorer from a job-listing dashboard into a decision-support cockpit: high information density, low cognitive friction, explicit evidence, absolute clarity about system state.

StatusProposed. No code, backlog or deployment changes are authorized by this document.
Section 02

The Four Questions

Every screen should let Tim answer these within seconds.

Q1
What needs my attention?
Q2
Which opportunities are worth pursuing?
Q3
Why does the system recommend that action?
Q4
What happened after I made a decision?
Section 03

Governing Principles

IDPrincipleMeaning
P1Trust before polishScores, counts, statuses and write confirmations are consistent and traceable.
P2Recognition over recallNo internal codes or cross-screen memory required.
P3Complexity on demandRoutine decisions simple; expert depth one step away, never removed.
P4Fast, reversible actionsFewest steps, protected against mistakes and failed writes.
P5Situational awarenessPreserve selection; explain changes; distinguish normal / pending / failed / unknown.
P6Operator controlAdaptive features recommend and organize; never silently override or rearrange.
P7Living, truthful HUDOperator design-authority decision (v1.3): rich motion wherever it helps — sliding, sweeping, materializing — running alongside instant actions and never hiding true state.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal03.1 · Binding Decisions
Section 03.1 · B-15 – B-17 new in v1.5.1

Binding Decisions (Tim; do not relitigate)

IDDecision
B-01Dense 11-column table stays the desktop default.
B-02Map stays prominent: permanent centre panel.
B-03Map shows only the selected job; else the current filtered set.
B-04Targeting look kept (reticle / lock-on, grid, coordinates, brackets). No radar sweep, range rings, clusters.
B-05Fullscreen map below the tab bar; ✕ Close + Esc always visible.
B-06Scoring page is a general scoring page; retain and enhance.
B-07Rich motion wherever it makes a little sense — the motion authority, within HF-15 limits.
B-08Desktop primary target 2560 × 1440.
B-09Separate iPhone 18 Pro redesign: portrait, landscape, desktop mode.
B-10Mobile: generous perimeter padding.
B-11Camera keep-out top (portrait), left or right (landscape).
B-12Duplicate tabs / cards / entry points consolidated.
B-13Black / neutral-grey military HUD; no blue tint.
B-14One-button updates with progress + Writer readback (on main, #112).
B-15Reduce motion: in-app toggle in Local preferences, OFF by default. If the OS reports prefers-reduced-motion, show a one-time prompt; never override silently. Every M-01..M-19 has a fully specified reduced equivalent (12.6).
B-16Event ticker: runs by default; visible, keyboard- and touch-operable Pause / Resume and Hide; choice persists locally; bot bursts deduplicated and throttled.
B-17Lock-on reticle keeps its circle (r22) and dashed outer circle (r31) as aiming marks: they never expand, sweep, pulse or encode distance. Range rings stay banned.
Doctrine. The governing UI rationale is v1.1 (AI Change Rationale — UI Design Reference Doctrine). This proposal cites no other doctrine version; motion authority is B-07 plus B-15 – B-17. Where the HCI review and Tim differ, Tim governs.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal04 · Research Basis
Section 04

Research Basis (correctly applied)

SourceApplication to Pipeline Explorer
Hick-HymanOrganize meaningful choices; don't strip options.
Working memoryMiller 1956; Cowan 2001 (~3–5 chunks). Minimize what must be remembered, not what is visible. Not a cap on screen elements.
FittsPrimary targets large and reachable; destructive actions separated.
Progressive disclosureFrequent functions exposed; specialist tools deferred.
GestaltGroup related data by spacing, alignment, consistent presentation.
Norman, emotional designVisceral = orderly industrial look; behavioral = reliable controls; reflective = confidence the system is right.
Feedback / visibilityNielsen heuristics: show true state and result of every action.
Adaptive UIsThe “81%” is the share of 211 studies (2012–2022) reporting some improvement — not an 81% gain. Treat as promising; test it.
NN/G data tablesDense professional tables are correct for find / compare / act on multivariate records.
Motion (operator decision)Tim explicitly chose a high-motion HUD as a design-authority decision (v1.3). Motion aids attention, continuity and change detection (NN/G animation guidance); guardrails keep it from blocking input, hiding state or flashing (WCAG 2.3.1).
How to read this basis. These findings justify organizing information, not removing it. Pipeline Explorer is an expert tool used daily; density is an asset when grouping, labeling and disclosure make it scannable. Every quantitative claim used in this proposal is stated with its correct scope.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal05 · Baseline Observations (1/2)
Section 05

Baseline Observations

Live build review (Oct 14) + read-only inventory (Oct 15, pre-#113 build) · corrected against main in 05.1 · bar colour = severity (red integrity, amber friction, green resolved)

Weights total is not honest
Settings › Flex policy & scoring: the weights card lists 70 (experience 35 · compensation 15 · geo 10 · title 5 · culture 5 · ats 0 · ownership 0) while FLEX 30 sits on another card. All eight weights belong to one shared model (rev 24, total 100); stale copy (“ranks rows on this browser”) made them look local. Corrected in v1.5.
Stored evidence is stale, not scores
Scores compute live from the published model. What goes stale is stored evidence: a live count (185 of 603 as of the Oct 15 03:00 ET inventory) of FLEX values stamped under an older DEGREE_FLEX rule; Writer-stamped values pending the Writer Apps Script redeploy. Anduril Head of Production 77 → 72 → 59 = FLEX class HIGH → NO (a legitimate evidence update) — shown with no cause. Reframed in v1.5.
Counts disagree across views
Declined by Tim 0 (Trends donut) / 56 (Scout results cohort) / 57 (Buckets table); Employer rejected 0 / 2 / 7; Applied 84 vs 26 (cohort). Scope labels (“live rows only”) are not shown next to the numbers.
Score inconsistency (v1.3)
Same job showed 75 (table) vs 68 “Watch” → 70 → 75 “Strong” (detail); three names for one number. Still open.
Writer status flapping
Red FAULT banner “Writer unreachable — Failed to fetch” on first load, then “Connected structured runtime”; Writer pill cycles checking / queued / processing / idle; drawer Health DEGRADED while listing no current faults.
Browsing is not side-effect free
Opening a job row queued a Writer write: drawer showed UNVERIFIED 1 write · oldest 65 s. Confirmed in code (v1.5): openRow() sets seen-state and calls syncStateUp(). Footer: “10 local entries · 10 unverified”.
Fullscreen map trap
Map (m=1) covers the section tabs with no visible close (one exists in the DOM, hidden); in My rulings the empty overlay “No mapped jobs in this group” blocks the tab bar. Exit only by reload. Header clipped under the rail; Layers click had no visible effect; Selection zoom 600 %.
Rail pin cannot unpin
Hamburger “Menu” pins the expanded rail; it overlaps the top-bar title and could not be collapsed again until reload.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal05 · Baseline Observations (2/2)
Section 05 · continued

Baseline Observations (2/2)

Duplicate entry points
Settings tabs Pay & location = anchor on Scoring; Resume & ATS = Documents. Cards PAY / GEO + SCORING, ATS TOOLS + DOCUMENTS, AI OPERATIONS + SCHEDULES open the same views. Writer setup via ⚙ and System › Writer connection. Writer pill, bell and rail Status all open the System drawer. System top tabs Schedules / Health repeat sub-tabs.
Scope copy is stale
Page copy says weights “rank rows on this browser”, but weights, salary curve, geo points and FLEX weight all publish to the one shared model (save_scoring_model). Truly local: display / columns, layout, map mode, seen-state, drafts. Badge PRESENTATION ONLY contradicts the shared Update buttons.
No real routes
All path routes (/scoring, /rules, /map, /trends …, even /zz-control-404) return 200 and silently redirect to /pipeline; state lives only in the URL hash.
Table overflow + codes
Jobs table truncated horizontally; ~150 fields; headers SALARY_BASE_EST, FLEX_CLASS, EXPERIENCE_FIT; states DECLINED_BY_TIM, INTAKE / AWAITING_ANALYSIS; reason codes FIT_TOO_WEAK etc.
Chart integrity
Discovery sources split by case: LinkedIn 183 + LINKEDIN 69, Indeed 87 + INDEED 17; Declined-by-Tim reason codes “none”.
Decision friction (v1.3)
Two-step decide (Pursue / Hold / Decline prepare, SAVE JOB DECISION commits); Decline adjacent to Pursue; UNDO only for the last decision.
Ops surfaces heavy
Daily job decisions share chrome with Dashboard KPIs, PR70 acceptance INDETERMINATE, Schedules UNSUPPORTED, Intake coverage UNKNOWN; Writer connection page shows Script URL + passphrase fields.
Runtime errors (v1.3)
Console TypeErrors at pipeline lines 1320 / 1326 — to be re-verified in Phase 0.
Performance
Selection ~0.55 s after the “memoize scoring config” fix (PR #113, 32 s → 0.7 s) — merged on main.

Every item is mapped to a requirement and an inventory task in Section 17.7. Each one is re-checked in Phase 0 (HF-14) before work starts.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal09 · Requirement Detail (1/4)
Section 09

Requirement Detail HF-01 – HF-04

HF-01One score, one meaningP0
  • Single scoring record: value, score type, rule/model version, computed-at, evidence status.
  • Queue, detail, map, compare render from that record. One display name everywhere.
  • Alternative / historical scores explicitly labeled, never silently substituted.
  • First suspect: the memoized scoring config (lag fix). Verify cache invalidation when the model is republished.
  • Dependency (v1.5): Writer-stamped values use the old formula until the Writer Apps Script is redeployed (Phase 0 discrepancy).
✓ Accept  Identical value and band for the same job / type / revision in every view.
HF-02Counts that reconcileP0
  • Each counter documents population, filters, time window, source. “Applied – all time” vs “Applied – this view” labeled.
  • Every Layer-1 tile is clickable and filters the queue to exactly its population.
  • Inventory cases: Declined by Tim 0 / 56 / 57 and Employer rejected 0 / 2 / 7 (Trends · Scout results · Buckets) carry explicit scope (live / cohort / archive).
✓ Accept  Every counter matches its documented query; tile click count == rows shown.
HF-03Decisions that show the truthP0
  • One click begins a write; no separate Save for routine decisions.
  • States: queued, processing, confirmed, failed, superseded. Receipt + Undo shown directly under the action buttons.
  • Writer is synchronous: a write lands in seconds; 30 s script lock; busy refusals auto-retry at 8 / 15 / 30 / 45 s. Queued state reads “◷ Waiting for Writer lock · N s”.
  • Failed (⊗) actions stay visible, keep payload, retry without duplicate canonical writes.
  • Confirmed only after readback; receipt bound to version + idempotency key (09.1).
  • Decline (⊖) writes only after a reason code; APPLIED / REJECTED_BY_EMPLOYER stay protected (#115).
✓ Accept  Simulated Writer failures never show success, never drop decisions, never duplicate rows.
HF-04Behavioral surprisesP1
  • Fix console errors (lines 1320 / 1326). Make Compact toggle work or remove it.
  • Settings shows one shared scoring model (all weights, salary, geo, FLEX weight) vs local display preferences; shared publishes warn and confirm.
  • Remove duplicate entry points: Settings tabs + cards, ⚙ vs Writer connection, three System-drawer triggers, Schedules / Health top tabs.
  • Writer banner / pill debounced (no “unreachable” flash on load); opening a job never causes a write.
v1.5.1 · Oct 15 2026 · Prepared for Tim PruittProposed — not authorized27 / 72
Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal09 · Requirement Detail (2/4)
Section 09 · continued

Requirement Detail HF-05 – HF-11

HF-05Context preservation and conflict guardP1
  • Refresh keeps selected job, filters, sort, scroll.
  • New / changed rows marked with a white Δ and neutral wipe (never cyan) instead of silent reorder; evidence updates state their cause.
  • If a bot changes the selected job after it was opened, warn before the decision commits; never overwrite silently.
HF-06NavigationP1
  • Map: permanent panel (HF-16); fullscreen sits below the tab bar with always-visible ✕ Close + Esc; auto-fit; selection synced with queue.
  • Rail never covers content (push, don't overlay); Menu pin toggles with a visible Unpin.
HF-07Density preservedP2
  • Keep 11-column desktop default; adjustable widths; column priority settings.
  • No horizontal overflow for priority columns (title, company, location, score, posted pay, age); clip nothing mid-word.
  • Target 15–20 visible rows at standard desktop viewport. Queue rows show posted pay + age next to score.
HF-08Readable labelsP2
  • SALARY_BASE_EST → “Base pay (est.)”; FLEX_CLASS → “Degree flex”; RESOLVED/APPLIED_CONFIRMED → “Applied – confirmed”. Raw codes live in Layer 4.
HF-09Score rationaleP2
  • One plain-English line next to every score (e.g., “Startup ramp role, $200–250K posted, degree required – flex”).
  • Breakdown and uncertainty one click away.
HF-10Change summaryP2
  • Strip: “Since your last review: N new · N scores changed (with cause, e.g. FLEX evidence HIGH → NO) · N Writer retries needed”, each item clickable.
HF-11Data integrity in chartsP2
  • Normalize source names case-insensitively; persist decline reason codes.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal09.1 · Decisions, Seen-state & Undo
Section 09.1 · new in v1.5.1

Decisions, Seen-state & Shared-model Undo

Decision receipts (HF-03 · C#06).
  • Each decision carries the record version seen at open and an idempotency key; the receipt is bound to both.
  • States: waiting for Writer lock → writing → confirmed only after Writer readback matches (never on transport acknowledgement) | failed (⊗) | superseded (record changed since open).
  • Undo is a verifiable inverse action on the confirmed state, itself receipted and read back; offered only while the record still holds the confirmed value.
  • Decline (⊖) starts its write only after a reason code is chosen.
  • APPLIED / REJECTED_BY_EMPLOYER protection unchanged (#115).
Seen-state (HF-04 · T-06 · C#07).
  • “Local-only” option removed. Opening a job is read-only at the moment of click.
  • Seen marks go into a debounced, idempotent batch sync (e.g. 10 s or 20 marks), separate from decisions and never blocking them.
  • Visible sync status (“Seen sync ✓ 14:32” / “◷ pending 3” / “⊗ failed · Retry”) with a repair path (retry, re-read server state).
  • NEW markers stay consistent across phone and desktop: server seen-state is authoritative; local queue merges by max timestamp.
Shared-model Undo (HF-19 · C#23).
  • Undo = restore the previous revision's settings as a NEW revision, sent with the current baseRevision.
  • Before restoring: show the current revision, the exact field diff (current → restored) and any intervening publishes.
  • Never roll back an intervening publish blindly; if the live revision moved, the dialog re-diffs against it.
  • Code fact: the Writer already rejects a publish built on an older or missing baseRevision (scoringPublishConflict_ → REVISION_CONFLICT). The UI surfaces that as “revision N is now live — review diff”.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal10–11 · Visual Standards, Color System
Section 10

Visual Standards

  • Black and neutral grey; no blue-tinted charcoal. Emphasis by contrast, weight, spacing, restrained status color.
  • Meaning = colour + unique glyph + word + position (never hue alone): green fits rules / top band; amber flex / waiting; red failed write or hard block only; clay low band; grey terminal.
  • Clear type hierarchy; minimize tiny text.
  • Rich motion by operator decision (v1.3): animate anywhere it makes a little sense — sliding, scrolling, sweeping, materializing — under the Motion System guardrails (Section 12).
  • Map style retained: the current military targeting look is design authority and is only enhanced (Section 13).
  • Visible focus, WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, logical keyboard order, keyboard shortcuts documented in a help overlay (not tiny inline text).
  • Emotional target: confidence and control in a living HUD — motion says the system is alive and working, never that it is unsure.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal11.7 · Percentile Population & Snapshot
Section 11.7 · new in v1.5.1

Percentile Population & Band Snapshot

RuleDefinition
PopulationEligible OPEN jobs in the master (OPEN preset definition). Fixed — never the current filter, view or search.
ExclusionsSTRICT FLEX / hard-blocked rows (shown ⊘ HOLD); applied, closed, declined, rejected, duplicates; rows with no score.
Denominator NCount of the population at snapshot time. Shown wherever bands are explained: “rank among N eligible open jobs · as of HH:MM”.
RanksPercentile rank = share of the population scoring strictly below + ½ ties; band from rank: ≥ P90 top · ≥ P65 upper · ≥ P20 mid · else low.
TiesEqual scores always take the higher band.
Minimum NIf N < 40, bands are hidden: rows show the numeric score only, plus “bands need ≥ 40 eligible open jobs (now N)”.
Out of populationApplied / closed rows show the numeric score with “— not ranked (applied)” / “(closed)”; HOLD rows show ⊘ HOLD; never a band colour.
SnapshotAtomic: {modelRev, populationRev, N, cutP90, cutP65, cutP20, asOf} published together; every view (table, ring, pins, compare, phone) renders from the same snapshot id. A new snapshot swaps in one frame — no split views, no arrival-order flashes.
RefreshOn model publish, evidence change or population change; at most once per 60 s otherwise.
MeaningBands are relative rank. The numeric score (absolute), fit and ⊘ HOLD stay visibly separate. The top band is never labelled “good fit”.
Tokens hold ranks, not scores. --pe-band-rank-top: 0.90 · -upper: 0.65 · -low: 0.20. Score cut-points are computed at runtime from the snapshot. Mock example only: N = 412, cut scores 61 / 54 / 38, top 76, median 48.
Live counts. Stale-evidence and other counts (e.g. “◌ 185 of 603”) are computed live and always carry “as of HH:MM”; mock figures in this document are labelled. Nothing is hard-coded in KPI, settings or acceptance.

Colour semanticsMeaning = colour + unique glyph + word + position. No state (success, failure, band, scope) conveyed by hue alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Replaces “one colour = one meaning”.C#09

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal12 · Motion System — Guardrails & Catalog
Section 12 · continued

Guardrails & Motion Catalog (1/2)

12.3 Guardrails — kept because they do not fight the standard
IDGuardrailRule
G1Never blocks inputActions dispatch at t = 0; animation runs alongside, is interruptible, and never gates a click, key or gesture. No “wait for animation” states.
G2Never hides true stateFinal values are in the DOM immediately; motion is a presentation layer. Write-state motion is driven only by state-machine events (Phase 1). If motion and state disagree, state wins and the animation is cancelled.
G360 fps, GPU onlyAnimate transform, opacity, filter (and SVG stroke-dashoffset on small elements). No layout properties. p95 frame ≤ 16.7 ms; concurrent animations capped (12 desktop / 6 phone); overflow degrades to fade.
G4Reduce motion toggle (B-15)Settings › Local preferences › Reduce motion, off by default (B-15); full reduced equivalents in 12.6. On: loops stop, slides become 120 ms fades, shake becomes a static outline. OS-level Reduce Motion triggers a one-time prompt; it never silently overrides Tim's choice.
G5Meaning conservedMotion colour follows signal meaning: amber breathe = waiting for Writer lock only, red shake = failed only, cyan = live / selected / writing; the changed marker is white, never cyan.
G6Flash safetyNothing flashes more than 3× per second (WCAG 2.3.1); confirmed flash is a single pulse.
G7Selection budget (v1.5)Job selection — data, detail materialize, ring, lock-on and auto-fit together — settles in ≤ 0.7 s total; anything longer is cut, not queued.
12.4 Catalog · every animation names its token
IDAnimationTriggerSpecification
M-01HUD boot-upApp loadGrid fades in → panels slide from edges → corner brackets draw → KPIs roll up → map auto-fits. 1200 ms total; any input skips it; controls live at t = 0.

M-03Job detail materializesSelectionScanline mask sweeps top → bottom with pixel-dissolve fade-in; cyan edge trace runs the panel border · materialize 400 ms. Real values from frame 1.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal12.5 · Selection Timeline, Loops & Ticker
Section 12.5 · new in v1.5.1

Selection Timeline, Loops & Ticker

JOB SELECTION · concurrency · total ≤ 700 ms p95 end to end (600+ rows)
t=0      click / key / tap
frame 1  data rendered: drawer values, ring number, row highlight, map pin — final + hit-testable
0–400    M-03 materialize (scanline + dissolve)       ┐
0–600    M-10 ring draw-on                            │ parallel, interruptible
0–300    M-04 auto-fit  300 ms on selection              │
60–300   M-05 lock-on   240 ms                         ┘
≤ 250    M-09 stagger total on selection; off for bursts or sets > 30 rows
≤ 700    settled — measured from input to last frame, p95, in CI (T-28)
Loops stop within 5 s (WCAG 2.2.2). “◷ Waiting for Writer lock” breathes for at most 5 s, then becomes steady amber + seconds counter + next-retry time (“◷ 12 s · next retry 15 s”). No loop anywhere runs past 5 s. Ticker is governed by B-16.
Event ticker (B-16 · C#04 / C#18). Runs by default. Visible ❚❚ Pause / ▶ Resume and Hide buttons (keyboard + touch, ≥ 24 px); choice persists locally; reading position kept on pause. Bot bursts deduplicated (same type within 60 s → one line “× n”) and throttled (≤ 1 new line / 4 s). Routine bot events muted. Secondary to the change strip.
Attention budget (C#18). The change strip is primary: grouped, clickable counts with causes. Ticker, row wipes and KPI rolls never compete for attention while a decision is open: during a decision the ticker freezes its scroll and new rows batch into the strip. Time-to-decision is measured with and without the ticker in HF-14.
Flash scheduler (C#12). Confirm pulses, scanlines and failure shakes are queued globally: ≥ 400 ms apart, max 3 / s whole-screen; extras degrade to static state. Verified by whole-screen capture.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal13 · Map System
Section 13

Map System · selected job, else filtered selection · targeting style

Purpose (design authority)
The pipeline map shows only the selected job's location, or — with nothing selected — the jobs in the current filtered selection (Jobs, Review queue, Decline candidates, My rulings + View & filters). Today's behaviour, Tim's binding rule.
Retained look
Black field, grey outlines, mono state labels, zoom readout, + / − / layers, RECENTER, RESET, legend, Home — current style, only enhanced.
Targeting layer
Reticle + crosshairs + corner-bracket lock-on on the selected job (M-05); HUD corner brackets on the panel; centre-of-view crosshair.
Grid & readouts
Graticule (1° minor, 5° major) with edge coordinates; selected job lat / long, range + bearing from Home, nearest geo control point and its score; cursor coordinates.
Pins
One pin per job in the filtered selection, coloured by percentile band (▲ Top · ◆ Upper · ● Mid · ▽ Low; ⊘ HOLD separate) with glyph + word + “rank among N eligible open · as of HH:MM” in the hover card; ◌ stale-evidence pins get an olive ring; remote jobs counted in the header.
Sync & auto-fit
Selection synced map ↔ queue ↔ drawer. Smooth animated auto-fit (M-04, 300 ms on selection): pans / zooms to the job, or to the bounds of the filtered set with padding — replaces the fixed 600 % selection zoom. Manual pan cancels; FIT re-fits.
Fullscreen
⤢ Fullscreen fills the workspace below the tab bar — never covers tabs or rail — with an always-visible ✕ Close · Esc top-right; selection, filter and viewport kept.
Removed (B-04 / B-17)
Radar sweep (map and loading), range rings + ticks (the lock-on r22 / r31 circles are aiming marks, not range rings), clusters, ping rings, dimmed filtered-out pins, dense-area boost — none serve “show where the job is”.
InteractionResult
Select row / click pinMap shows only that job; auto-fit pans / zooms to it (M-04); lock-on runs (M-05); drawer materializes (M-03).
Clear selection · EscReturns to the filtered selection; auto-fit to its bounds; pins enter with a short drop (M-06).
Filter / preset changePin set = new filter result exactly (no dimmed leftovers); header count rolls (M-07); auto-fit.
⤢ Fullscreen / ✕ CloseExpands below the tab bar (M-16); ✕ Close and Esc always visible; never a trap, also in empty views (“No mapped jobs in this group”).

Mobile Redesign — iPhone 18 Pro

Safe areas ≈ 62 top / 34 bottom (portrait), 62 each side / 21 bottom (landscape). Not confirmed for this model — verify in the simulator; layout derives from safe-area insets, not constants.
16.0 Perimeter & keep-out rules (v1.4 — Tim)
TokenValueRule
--pe-safe-*env(safe-area-inset-*)Always read from the OS — never hard-coded (assumed 62 / 34 portrait, 62 / 62 / 21 landscape).

--pe-pad-corner36ptSide inset for any control inside a corner zone (top / bottom 96 pt), clear of the ≈ 55 pt display radius (tab bar x 36–366).

  • KPI strip (Decide · New · Failed · ◌ Provisional) + change strip, inside the 24 pt padding.

Implementation Plan — Overview

AuthorizationThis plan is proposed only. No code, backlog or deployment changes are authorized by this document; each phase starts only on Tim's explicit approval. In scope: UI that lets Tim make shared model / rule changes safely. Out of scope in every phase: agents changing the shared model or rules.

Sequence and gates

#PhaseRequirementsObjectiveExit gate
00BaselineHF-14Measured baseline of 5 real review tasks.Baseline report + discrepancy register signed off.
01IntegrityHF-01 · 02 · 03 · 04 · 19 (data)One score, reconciled counts, truthful writes (seconds-scale), ◌ stale evidence, honest all-SHARED weights, no write on view. Data fixes only.No unexplained cross-view discrepancy; zero false successes.
1BArchitecture & performanceHF-01 · 03 · 15 (limits)Single scoring-record selector, counter registry module, write state machine, browser-test migration, performance budget (≤ 0.7 s selection, p95 ≤ 16.7 ms).Perf + test suite green; budget enforced in CI.
02Workflow + motion coreHF-04 · 05 · 06 · 15 (core) · 16 (panel)Context survives refresh; map per Tim's rule + fullscreen close; scope badges + shared-change guard; de-duplicated entry points; motion core.Refresh keeps context; motion never blocks input.
03Cognitive + visual + 2560HF-07 – 11 · 15 – 17 · 19 + tokens2560 cockpit, full motion catalog, scoring page + geo map, palette.Measured faster review, no accuracy loss; 60 fps.
04AdaptiveHF-12Opt-in, explainable personalization.Explainable, reversible, subordinate to canonical rules and Tim's decisions.
MMobile trackHF-13 · 18iPhone portrait / landscape / desktop-mode with perimeter insets + camera keep-out; after Phase 2 gate, parallel to Phase 3.Swipe decisions reversible; state kept across switch.

Section 17 · continued

Sequencing & Cross-cutting Constraints

PHASE            ────────────────────────────── time ──────────────────────────────▶
00 Baseline      ████
01 Integrity         ██████████  ◀ data fixes only
1B Arch + perf                ██████  ◀ no motion / layout before this gate

Writer timing (seconds). Writer is synchronous Apps Script: a write lands in seconds; a 30 s script lock refuses concurrent writes; the client auto-retries at 8 / 15 / 30 / 45 s. Queued = “waiting for Writer lock · N s”, never a fault until retries are exhausted (⊗ failed).
Writer redeploy dependency. The updated Writer Apps Script is not yet deployed; Writer-stamped values use the old formula until it is. Logged in Phase 0; HF-01 consistency gate cannot pass before redeploy.
Multi-bot edits. Each decision carries the record version seen at open; a mismatch triggers the conflict guard (HF-05) and a superseded state. Bulk bot updates summarize in the change strip and ticker rather than individually animating.
Design authority. Layout follows Tim's v1.4 / v1.5 decisions: 2560 three-zone cockpit; map shows the selected job or the filtered set in its targeting style (no radar); high-motion standard; scoring page retained as authority. Further layout changes need Tim's explicit approval. UI for Tim's shared changes is in scope; agents changing the model or rules is not.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal17 · Phase 0 — Baseline
Section 17.1
00BaselineHF-14
Objective
Measure the current build before anything changes, so every later gate is judged against real numbers rather than impressions.
Tasks
  1. Script 5 representative review tasks: (a) find the job that needs action, (b) state the main score drivers for a given job, (c) disposition a straightforward job, (d) reconcile the Applied count, (e) find the previously selected job after a refresh.
  2. Run each task on the live build across at least 3 sessions; record completion time, errors, extra navigation, scrolling, and perceived difficulty (1–7 single-ease question).
  3. Snapshot score value, band and label for 20 sample jobs in table, detail, map and compare views, with timestamps.
  4. Snapshot every counter (header, KPI tiles, Trends) with the query it appears to represent; log mismatches (Applied 84 vs 26, Declined 57 vs 56, intake 0 vs 138, “0 need you” vs 50).
  5. Capture console logs (TypeErrors at lines 1320 / 1326), selection latency (~0.55s), and an inventory of raw internal codes visible in Layers 1–3.
  6. Record Writer lock refusals and retry counts (8 / 15 / 30 / 45 s) per session.
  7. Discrepancy (v1.5): Writer Apps Script redeploy outstanding — Writer-stamped values on the old formula; note as an HF-01 dependency.
Deliverables
  • Baseline report (timings, errors, difficulty)
  • Discrepancy register: scores and counters
  • Reusable task scripts for each re-test
Exit gate · acceptance tests
  • All 5 tasks timed in ≥ 3 sessions
  • Discrepancy register reviewed and signed off by Tim
  • No product changes made during the phase
Risks & mitigations
  • Bots change data mid-session → timestamp every snapshot and note Writer lock state.
  • Small sample → report medians and ranges; treat targets as directional, not statistical proof.
v1.5.1 · Oct 15 2026 · Prepared for Tim PruittProposed — not authorized60 / 72
Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal17 · Phase 1 — Integrity
Section 17.2
01IntegrityHF-01HF-02HF-03HF-04HF-19
Objective
Make every number, count and decision state truthful and identical everywhere before improving anything else.
Tasks
  1. Define the single scoring record {value, score type, rule/model version, computed-at, evidence status}; route queue, detail, map and compare through one selector.
  2. Audit the memoized scoring config: key the cache on a rules/weights version hash and invalidate on change, keeping the ≤ 0.7s selection budget.
  3. Adopt one display name for the score; label any historical or alternative score explicitly.
  4. Write a counter registry (population, filters, window, source) for every Layer-1 tile and header count; each tile applies that exact query to the queue.
  5. Implement a one-click decision state machine: queued → processing → confirmed | failed | superseded, with an idempotency key per decision.
  6. Show receipt + Undo under the buttons; queued shows “waiting for Writer lock · N s” with the next retry; failed (⊗) keeps its payload and offers Retry.
  7. Fix console TypeErrors at pipeline lines 1320 / 1326.
  8. Expose state-machine events as the only source for write-state motion later (G2).
  9. Stale evidence (HF-19): record carries model rev + evidence status; ◌ on every stale evidence value (live count + as-of); evidence-driven changes logged with cause (Anduril 77 → 72 → 59, FLEX HIGH → NO).
  10. Honest weights: one all-SHARED table summing to 100 (rev 24) on Settings and in Fit & Score (copy + FLEX row done in #116); reconcile Declined 0 / 56 / 57 and Employer rejected 0 / 2 / 7.
  11. Opening a job is read-only at click; seen marks batch-synced (09.1); debounce the Writer banner / pill (2 failed checks or 20 s grace).
Deliverables
  • Scoring record spec + single selector
  • Counter registry document
  • Decision state machine with receipts
  • Fault-injection test suite
Exit gate · acceptance tests
  • Cross-view score consistency 100% on all jobs
  • Counter reconciliation 100%; tile click count == rows shown
  • Fault injection (timeout, 5xx, duplicate ack, lock busy): 0 false successes, 0 dropped, 0 duplicates
  • Console clean across the 5 task scripts
  • ◌ on 100 % of stale evidence; weights total = visible sum, all SHARED
Risks & mitigations
  • Lock contention looks “stuck” → seconds timer + next-retry countdown.
  • Cache fix reintroduces the 32s lag → selection performance test in the gate.
  • Multi-bot edits during a write → superseded state, never overwrite.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal17 · Phase 1B — Architecture & Performance
Section 17.3
1BArchitecture & performanceHF-01HF-03HF-15
Objective
Put the structure in place that motion and layout depend on, with an enforced performance budget. Starts after the Phase 1 gate; motion and layout start only after this gate.
Tasks
  1. Single scoring-record selector module; every view reads through it; memo keyed on model revision.
  2. Counter registry as code (population, filters, window, source) with unit tests.
  3. Write state machine (waiting for lock → writing → confirmed | failed | superseded) as one module; motion subscribes to its events only.
  4. Migrate browser tests to the current build (PRs #111–#115) incl. protected APPLIED / REJECTED_BY_EMPLOYER and score-tester flows.
  5. Performance budget in CI: selection ≤ 0.7 s end to end, p95 frame ≤ 16.7 ms, concurrent-animation caps, no layout-property animation.
  6. Flash audit harness: whole-screen capture, nothing > 3 flashes / s; loops stop ≤ 5 s.
  7. Gate entry: second HCI review (ChatGPT) of v1.5.1 completed and reviewed by Tim.
Deliverables
  • Selector + registry + state-machine modules
  • Updated browser test suite
  • Perf budget + CI trace
Exit gate · acceptance tests
  • All browser tests green on main
  • Selection ≤ 0.7 s p95 end to end with 600+ rows over 50 selections
  • p95 frame ≤ 16.7 ms in a scripted motion trace
  • Tim reviews the gate
Risks & mitigations
  • Refactor regresses #113 lag fix → perf test is a gate.
  • Scope creep into UI → no visual changes in this phase.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal17 · Phase 2 — Workflow
Section 17.4
02WorkflowHF-04HF-05HF-06HF-15HF-16HF-19
Objective
Remove behavioral surprises, make context survive every refresh, make the map a permanent panel, and ship the motion core.
Tasks
  1. Make the Compact toggle work or remove it.
  2. Second HCI gate (ChatGPT) on v1.5.1 before Phase 1B starts.
  3. Preserve selected job, filters, sort and scroll across refresh using stable job IDs.
  4. New / changed rows get the neutral wipe (M-08) and a white Δ marker instead of silent reorder; bulk bot updates batch into the change strip.
  5. Conflict guard: store record version on open; on mismatch at commit, show what changed and require confirmation.
  6. Map per Tim's rule (HF-16): selected job only, else the filtered set; animated auto-fit; fullscreen below tabs with visible ✕ Close + Esc; remove radar, rings, clusters.
  7. Scope + shared-change guard (HF-19): SHARED on all scoring cards, LOCAL only on display prefs; confirm + receipt + Undo (= republish previous revision) for every shared publish.
  8. App-wide fixes (T-08 – T-13, T-20 – T-22): rail Unpin, de-duplicated tabs / cards / drawer entries, ⚙ → Settings, path aliases, bulk-action confirm.
  9. Motion tokens file + core transitions (HF-15): panel slide, tab slide, toast slide-up, write-state pulses bound to Phase 1 events; Reduce motion toggle (off by default).
  10. Sidebar rail pushes content rather than overlaying it.
Deliverables
  • Scope + guard spec
  • Context preservation + conflict guard
  • Map rule + motion core
Exit gate · acceptance tests
  • Selection retained after refresh 100% over 50 refresh cycles
  • Simulated bot edit mid-decision always warns; never overwrites
  • Map collapse found unaided; selection sync 100%
  • Motion never blocks input (dispatch ≤ 50 ms)
  • HF-14 re-test shows no regressions
Risks & mitigations
  • Highlight noise during bulk bot activity → batch and summarize.
  • Motion masking state → G2: state wins, animation cancels.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal18 · Design Tokens — Colour & Shape
Section 18

Design Tokens (CSS)

Phase 2 ships motion tokens; Phase 3 applies colour, motion and breakpoint tokens through a single token file. Motion and breakpoints continue on the next page. Components reference tokens only; a lint rule rejects raw hex values elsewhere. Semantic aliases (e.g. --pe-state-failed: var(--pe-red)) may be added; meaning is carried by colour + glyph + word + position, never hue alone.

/* Pipeline Explorer — design tokens (proposed) */
:root {
  /* Base surfaces */
  --pe-void:            #000000;  /* page background */
  --pe-hull:            #0B0B0B;  /* panels */
  --pe-plate:           #141414;  /* cards / rows */
  --pe-raised:          #1E1E1E;  /* hover / selected */
  --pe-seam:            #2A2A2A;  /* borders */
  --pe-gridline:        #3A3A3A;  /* map grid */
  /* Text */
  --pe-text-primary:    #E6E6E2;
  --pe-text-secondary:  #A3A39E;
  --pe-text-muted:      #6B6B66;  /* large text only; never 11 px headers or ◌ */
  /* Signal */
  --pe-green:           #4ADE80;  /* fits / confirmed / Pursue */
  --pe-amber:           #F2B33D;  /* flex / waiting for lock / Hold */
  --pe-red:             #FF4D3D;  /* failed write / hard block only */
  --pe-cyan:            #38E1D6;  /* selection / focus / links */
  --pe-olive:           #8A8F7A;  /* discovery / unverified */
  --pe-terminal:        #5A5A5A;  /* decoration beside a word only (2.67:1 on Plate) */
  /* Percentile bands (v1.5, display-only) */
  --pe-band-top:        #4ADE80;  /* top 10 % */
  --pe-band-upper:      #F2B33D;  /* next 25 % */
  --pe-band-mid:        #8E8E89;  /* next 45 % */
  --pe-band-low:        #D9826B;  /* bottom 20 % (Clay) */
  --pe-band-rank-top:   0.90;  /* P90 percentile rank */
  --pe-band-rank-upper: 0.65;  /* P65 */
  --pe-band-rank-low:   0.20;  /* P20 */
  --pe-band-min-n:      40;  /* hide bands below */
  /* Shape, glow, type, targets */
  --pe-border:          1px solid var(--pe-seam);
  --pe-radius:          2px;
  --pe-bar:             2px;  /* signal left bar */
  --pe-bar-card:        3px;  /* card signal bar */
  --pe-focus-ring:      2px solid #E6E6E2;  /* + 2px Void offset */
  --pe-glow:            0 0 6px rgba(56,225,214,0.40);  /* focus + processing only */
  --pe-font-label:      "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, monospace;  /* uppercase labels */
  --pe-font-ui:         "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;  /* numbers / titles */
  --pe-target-min:      44pt;  /* phone targets */
  --pe-target-decision: 52pt;  /* phone Pursue / Hold */
  /* Scope &amp; markers (v1.5) */
  --pe-scope-shared:    var(--pe-amber);  /* SHARED badge */
  --pe-scope-local:     var(--pe-text-secondary);  /* LOCAL (display only) */
  --pe-changed:         #E6E6E2;  /* Δ marker, never cyan */
  --pe-stale-evidence:  var(--pe-olive);  /* ◌ stale stored evidence */
}
Glow: box-shadow: var(--pe-glow) on focus, processing, traces and lock-on; nothing glows at rest.
Signals as accents: border-left: var(--pe-bar) solid var(--pe-amber); never a background fill.

Section 18 · continued

Design Tokens — Motion, Breakpoints, Layout

/* PE tokens · v1.5.1 */
:root {
  /* Motion — durations */
  --pe-motion-instant:         0ms;
  --pe-motion-fast:            120ms;
  --pe-motion-base:            240ms;
  --pe-motion-lock:            240ms;
  --pe-motion-materialize:     400ms;
  --pe-motion-sweep:           600ms;
  --pe-motion-roll:            800ms;
  --pe-motion-boot:            1200ms;
  --pe-motion-breathe:         1600ms;
  --pe-motion-fit:             300ms;
  --pe-motion-fit-set:         600ms;
  --pe-loop-max:               5s;
  --pe-stagger-max:            250ms;
  --pe-motion-stagger:         18ms;
  --pe-select-budget:          700ms;
  --pe-frame-p95:              16.7ms;
  --pe-flash-max:              3;
  /* Motion — easing */
  --pe-ease-out:               cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);
  --pe-ease-in:                cubic-bezier(.7,0,.84,0);
  --pe-ease-inout:             cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1);
  --pe-ease-snap:              cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1);
  --pe-ease-linear:            linear;
  /* Breakpoints */
  --pe-bp-desktop-2560:        2560px;
  --pe-bp-desktop-1920:        1920px;
  --pe-bp-desktop-1440:        1440px;
  --pe-bp-phone-portrait:      402pt;
  --pe-bp-phone-landscape:     874pt;
  /* Layout @ 2560 */
  --pe-margin:                 20px;
  --pe-gutter:                 16px;
  --pe-col-rail:               56px;
  --pe-col-table:              1112px;
  --pe-col-map:                800px;
  --pe-col-work:               508px;
  --pe-row-h:                  32px;
  /* Mobile perimeter (v1.4) */
  --pe-pad-side:               24pt;
  --pe-pad-corner:             36pt;
  --pe-pad-top:                12pt;
  --pe-lift-bottom:            16pt;
  --pe-island-clear:           16pt;
  --pe-pad-land:               20pt;
}

Phone breakpoints are assumed iPhone 18 Pro dimensions (Section 16); 2560 is the primary desktop target.

/* layout selection */
@media (min-width: 2560px) { .cockpit { grid-template-columns: var(--pe-col-rail) var(--pe-col-table) var(--pe-col-map) var(--pe-col-work); } }
@media (max-width: 440px) and (orientation: portrait)  { .app { --layout: mobile-portrait; } }
@media (max-height: 440px) and (orientation: landscape) { .app { --layout: mobile-landscape; } }
.app[data-desktop-mode] { --layout: desktop-2560; /* scaled, pannable */ }
[data-reduce-motion] { /* B-15: off by default; full table in 12.6 */ --pe-motion-breathe: 0ms; --pe-motion-fit: 0ms; --pe-motion-lock: 0ms; --pe-motion-sweep: 0ms; --pe-motion-roll: 0ms; --pe-motion-stagger: 0ms; }
.app { padding: calc(env(safe-area-inset-top) + var(--pe-pad-top)) calc(env(safe-area-inset-right) + var(--pe-pad-side)) calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + var(--pe-lift-bottom)) calc(env(safe-area-inset-left) + var(--pe-pad-side)); }
Lint: no raw durations, easing curves or radar tokens in components — only --pe-motion-* and --pe-ease-*, mirroring the raw-hex rule.
Reduce motion (B-15: Local preferences, off by default; OS preference prompts once) applies the 12.6 table.

Pipeline Explorer // Human Factors Proposal20–21 · References, Design Standard
Section 20

References

  • Nielsen, 10 Usability Heuristics (NN/G, rev. 2024)
  • Nielsen, Progressive Disclosure (NN/G, 2006)
  • Laubheimer, Data Tables: Four Major User Tasks (NN/G, 2022)
  • Cowan, The Magical Number 4 (2001)
  • Norman, Emotional Design (2004 / 2008)
  • Intelligent User Interfaces and Their Evaluation (systematic mapping, 211 studies, PMC)
  • W3C, WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum); SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes
  • Harley, The Role of Animation and Motion in UX (NN/G, 2014)
  • Apple, Human Interface Guidelines — layout, safe areas, haptics
Section 21

Design Standard (controlling statement)

Pipeline Explorer shall be an expert decision-support system that minimizes cognitive translation, preserves situational awareness, provides truthful system feedback, and supports rapid, recoverable actions. It shall keep authoritative data consistent across views, preserve user context during updates, and expose decision evidence without unnecessary navigation. Progressive disclosure organizes complexity; it does not remove necessary information. Adaptive functionality stays transparent, explainable, reversible and under user control. By operator decision, motion is a first-class element — rich and continuous, yet never blocking input or concealing true state — the tactical map is a primary panel in its retained military targeting style that shows only the selected job or the current filtered selection, and the scoring page stays the authority for how scores are set, with every local or shared change scoped, previewed and reversible. All changes preserve established design authority unless explicitly approved, and are validated against usability, accessibility and data-integrity criteria.
StatusProposed · v1.5.1 · October 15, 2026. A second HCI gate (ChatGPT) runs before Phase 1B; Tim has final authority. No code, backlog or deployment changes authorized.
